وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَنِّي حِينَئِذٍ بَرِيئَةٌ، وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُبَرِّئِي بِبَرَاءَتِي وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ مَا كُنْتُ أَظُنُّ أَنَّ اللَّهَ مُنْزِلٌ فِي شَأْنِي وَحْيًا يُتْلَى، لَشَأْنِي فِي نَفْسِي كَانَ أَحْقَرَ مِنْ أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ فِيَّ بِأَمْرٍ، وَلَكِنْ كُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَرَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي النَّوْمِ رُؤْيَا يُبَرِّئُنِي اللَّهُ بِهَا، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَجْلِسَهُ، وَلاَ خَرَجَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ، حَتَّى أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَخَذَهُ مَا كَانَ يَأْخُذُهُ مِنَ الْبُرَحَاءِ، حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيَتَحَدَّرُ مِنْهُ مِنَ الْعَرَقِ مِثْلُ الْجُمَانِ وَهْوَ فِي يَوْمٍ شَاتٍ، مِنْ ثِقَلِ الْقَوْلِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ـ قَالَتْ ـ فَسُرِّيَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهْوَ يَضْحَكُ، فَكَانَتْ أَوَّلَ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا أَنْ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ أَمَّا اللَّهُ فَقَدْ بَرَّأَكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَقَالَتْ لِي أُمِّي قُومِي إِلَيْهِ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَقُومُ إِلَيْهِ، فَإِنِّي لاَ أَحْمَدُ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ـ قَالَتْ ـ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏[quran sura="24" aya_start="11" aya_end="22"]{‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالإِفْكِ‏}‏ الْعَشْرَ الآيَاتِ، ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذَا فِي بَرَاءَتِي‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ـ وَكَانَ يُنْفِقُ عَلَى مِسْطَحِ بْنِ أُثَاثَةَ لِقَرَابَتِهِ مِنْهُ وَفَقْرِهِ ـ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُنْفِقُ عَلَى مِسْطَحٍ شَيْئًا أَبَدًا بَعْدَ الَّذِي قَالَ لِعَائِشَةَ مَا قَالَ‏.‏ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ [quran sura="24" aya_start="22" aya_end="22"]‏{‏ وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ أُولُو الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ‏}‏ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ بَلَى وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأُحِبُّ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لِي فَرَجَعَ إِلَى مِسْطَحٍ النَّفَقَةَ الَّتِي كَانَ يُنْفِقُ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَنْزِعُهَا مِنْهُ أَبَدًا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ سَأَلَ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتَ جَحْشٍ عَنْ أَمْرِي فَقَالَ لِزَيْنَبَ مَاذَا عَلِمْتِ أَوْ رَأَيْتِ فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَحْمِي سَمْعِي وَبَصَرِي وَاللَّهِ مَا عَلِمْتُ إِلَّا خَيْرًا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ وَهِيَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ تُسَامِينِي مِنْ أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَعَصَمَهَا اللَّهُ بِالْوَرَعِ قَالَتْ وَطَفِقَتْ أُخْتُهَا حَمْنَةُ تُحَارِبُ لَهَا فَهَلَكَتْ فِيمَنْ هَلَكَ قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ فَهَذَا الَّذِي بَلَغَنِي مِنْ حَدِيثِ هَؤُلَاءِ الرَّهْطِ ثُمَّ قَالَ عُرْوَةُ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُ مَا قِيلَ لَيَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ مَا كَشَفْتُ مِنْ كَنَفِ أُنْثَى قَطُّ قَالَتْ ثُمَّ قُتِلَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ
en_text: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud narrated to me, from ‘Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning what the people of the slander said about her. Each of them told me part of her account. Some had retained her account better than others and remembered it more firmly. I retained from each man the report he narrated to me from ‘Aishah, and parts of their reports confirmed one another, even though some had retained more than others. They said that ‘Aishah said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended to travel, he drew lots among his wives. Whichever wife’s lot came out, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would take her with him. On one expedition he undertook, he drew lots among us and my lot came out. I went with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, after the veil had been prescribed. I was carried in my howdah and put down in it. We travelled until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished that expedition and was returning. When we had drawn near Madinah on our return, he announced one night that we would set off. I got up when they announced our departure and walked past the army. When I had finished what I needed to do, I returned to my riding place and felt my chest. My necklace, made of beads from Zafar, had broken. I went back to look for it, and searching for it delayed me. The group of men who used to prepare me for travel came and lifted my howdah, placed it on the camel I rode, and set it off, thinking I was inside it. At that time women were light in weight. They had not grown heavy or been covered with flesh; they ate only a little food. So the people did not notice how light the howdah was when they lifted and carried it. I was a young girl. They sent the camel on and continued. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their stopping places, but there was no caller or responder among them. I went to the place where I had been staying and thought that they would notice I was missing and return for me. While I was sitting there, sleep overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu‘attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had been behind the army. In the morning he reached the place where I was and saw the dark outline of a sleeping person. He recognized me when he saw me, because he had seen me before the veil was prescribed. I woke when he said, ‘We belong to Allah, and to Him we return.’ When he recognized me, I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, we did not exchange a single word, and I heard no word from him except that phrase. He made his camel kneel, pressed its foreleg down, and I got up and mounted it. He then led the camel with me until we reached the army in the heat of midday, while they were stopped to rest. ‘Aishah said: Some people were ruined because of me, and the one who took the leading part in the slander was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. ‘Urwah said: I was informed that the story used to be spread and discussed in his presence, and that he approved of it, listened to it, and sought it out. ‘Urwah also said: Among the people of the slander, only Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh were named to me, along with other people about whom I have no knowledge. They were a group, as Allah Most High said, and the one said to have borne the greatest share of it was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. ‘Urwah said: ‘Aishah disliked having Hassan insulted in her presence. She would say that he was the one who said, “My father, his father, and my honor are a shield for Muhammad’s honor against you.” ‘Aishah said: When we arrived in Madinah, I became ill for a month. People were discussing what the slanderers had said, but I knew nothing about it. What troubled me during my illness was that I no longer received from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only come in, greet me, and say, “How is that one?” Then he would leave. That troubled me, though I did not know of the evil being said, until I had recovered. Then I went out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi‘, our place for relieving ourselves. We used to go out only from one night to the next. This was before we had latrines near our homes. Our practice was like that of the early Arabs in the open country, and we disliked having latrines near our houses. Umm Mistah and I set out. She was the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn ‘Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn ‘Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn ‘Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. When Umm Mistah and I were returning toward my home after finishing what we needed to do, she stumbled over her cloak and said, “May Mistah be ruined!” I said to her, “What a terrible thing to say! Are you insulting a man who was present at Badr?” She said, “You poor woman, have you not heard what he said?” I asked, “What did he say?” Then she told me what the people of the slander had said. ‘Aishah said: My illness grew worse. When I returned home, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in, greeted me, and said, “How is that one?” I said, “Will you let me go to my parents?” I wanted to make sure of the report from them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave me permission. I said to my mother, “Mother, what are people talking about?” She said, “My daughter, take it lightly. By Allah, it is rare for a beautiful woman who is loved by a man and has co-wives not to have them speak against her.” I said, “Glory be to Allah! Are people really talking about this?” I cried through that night until morning. My tears would not stop, and I could not sleep. In the morning I was still crying. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation had been delayed, to ask their advice about separating from his wife. Usamah advised him according to what he knew of his family’s innocence and the affection he knew the Prophet held for them. Usamah said, “They are your family, and we know nothing about them except good.” ‘Ali said, “Messenger of Allah, Allah has not placed any restriction on you. There are many women besides her. Ask the servant girl and she will tell you the truth.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for Barirah and said, “Barirah, have you seen anything that makes you doubt her?” Barirah said, “By the One who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her that I could criticize, except that she is a young girl who sometimes falls asleep while her family’s dough is rising, and then the household animal comes and eats it.” ‘Aishah said: That day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood up on the pulpit and sought support against ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. He said, “Muslims, who will help me against a man whose harm to my family has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing about my family except good. They have also mentioned a man about whom I know nothing except good, and he never entered my family’s home except when he was with me.” ‘Aishah said: Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh, the brother of Banu ‘Abd al-Ashhal, stood up and said, “Messenger of Allah, I will help you. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; if he is one of our brothers from the Khazraj, command us and we will carry out your command.” A man from the Khazraj then stood up. Hassan’s mother was his paternal cousin from his branch. It was Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj. ‘Aishah said: He had previously been a righteous man, but tribal zeal overcame him. He said to Sa‘d, “By the life of Allah, you have lied. You will not kill him, and you are not able to kill him. If he were from your own clan, you would not want him killed.” Usayd ibn Hudayr, who was Sa‘d’s cousin, stood up and said to Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, “By the life of Allah, you have lied. We will kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of the hypocrites.” ‘Aishah said: The two clans, Aws and Khazraj, became stirred up until they were about to fight, while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was standing on the pulpit. He kept calming them until they fell silent, and then he was silent. ‘Aishah said: I cried that whole day, with tears that would not stop and without sleeping. The next morning my parents were with me. I had cried for two nights and a day, with tears that would not stop and without sleeping, until I thought the crying would split my liver. While my parents were sitting with me and I was crying, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to come in. I let her in, and she sat and cried with me. While we were like that, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in, greeted us, and sat down. He had not sat with me since people first said what they said about me. A month had passed without any revelation being sent to him concerning me. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, bore witness, then said, “To continue: ‘Aishah, I have heard such-and-such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare you innocent. If you have committed a sin, ask Allah for forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant admits a sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance.” ‘Aishah said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished speaking, my tears dried up until I could no longer feel a single drop. I said to my father, “Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.” My father said, “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.” I said to my mother, “Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.” My mother said, “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.” I said, “I am a young girl and do not recite much of the Quran. By Allah, I know that you have heard this story until it settled in your hearts and you believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me. But if I admit something to you, while Allah knows I am innocent of it, you will believe me. By Allah, I can find no example for you and me except the father of Yusuf, who said, ‘So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe’ (12:18).” Then I turned over and lay on my bed. Allah knew that I was innocent then, and that Allah would declare me innocent. But by Allah, I did not think Allah would send down revelation about me that would be recited. My situation seemed too insignificant to me for Allah to speak about it. I had only hoped that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would see a dream in which Allah declared me innocent. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not left his seat, and no one from the household had gone out, when revelation came down to him. The state that used to overcome him came over him, until sweat like pearls ran down from him, even on a cold day, because of the weight of the words revealed to him. When that state passed from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he was smiling. The first words he said were, “Aishah, Allah has declared you innocent.” My mother said to me, “Get up and go to him.” I said, “By Allah, I will not get up to go to him. I will praise none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” ‘Aishah said: Allah Most High revealed the ten verses beginning, “Indeed, those who brought the slander,” concerning my innocence (24:11–22). Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who used to support Mistah ibn Uthathah because of their kinship and his poverty, said, “By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah again after what he said about ‘Aishah.” Then Allah revealed, “Those of you who possess grace and abundance should not swear…” up to the words, “…All-Forgiving, Most Merciful” (24:22). Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said, “Indeed, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me.” So he resumed the support he had been giving Mistah and said, “By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him.” ‘Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about me. He said to Zaynab, “What have you known or seen?” She said, “Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing about her except good.” ‘Aishah said: She was the one among the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who used to compete with me for his favor, but Allah protected her through her piety. Her sister Hamnah began defending her, and she was among those who perished. Ibn Shihab said: This is what reached me from the reports of these men. Then ‘Urwah said: ‘Aishah said, “By Allah, the man about whom people said what they said would say, ‘Glory be to Allah! By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I have never uncovered any woman’s covering.’” ‘Aishah said: He was later killed in the cause of Allah.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4418, book 64, باب حَدِيثُ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا اللَّيْثُ، عَنْ عُقَيْلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ـ وَكَانَ قَائِدَ كَعْبٍ مِنْ بَنِيهِ حِينَ عَمِيَ ـ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ كَعْبَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، يُحَدِّثُ حِينَ تَخَلَّفَ عَنْ قِصَّةِ، تَبُوكَ قَالَ كَعْبٌ لَمْ أَتَخَلَّفْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي غَزْوَةٍ غَزَاهَا إِلاَّ فِي غَزْوَةِ تَبُوكَ، غَيْرَ أَنِّي كُنْتُ تَخَلَّفْتُ فِي غَزْوَةِ بَدْرٍ، وَلَمْ يُعَاتِبْ أَحَدًا تَخَلَّفَ، عَنْهَا إِنَّمَا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُرِيدُ عِيرَ قُرَيْشٍ، حَتَّى جَمَعَ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ عَدُوِّهِمْ عَلَى غَيْرِ مِيعَادٍ وَلَقَدْ شَهِدْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيْلَةَ الْعَقَبَةِ حِينَ تَوَاثَقْنَا عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ، وَمَا أُحِبُّ أَنَّ لِي بِهَا مَشْهَدَ بَدْرٍ، وَإِنْ كَانَتْ بَدْرٌ أَذْكَرَ فِي النَّاسِ مِنْهَا، كَانَ مِنْ خَبَرِي أَنِّي لَمْ أَكُنْ قَطُّ أَقْوَى وَلاَ أَيْسَرَ حِينَ تَخَلَّفْتُ عَنْهُ فِي تِلْكَ الْغَزْوَةِ، وَاللَّهِ مَا اجْتَمَعَتْ عِنْدِي قَبْلَهُ رَاحِلَتَانِ قَطُّ حَتَّى جَمَعْتُهُمَا فِي تِلْكَ الْغَزْوَةِ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُرِيدُ غَزْوَةً إِلاَّ وَرَّى بِغَيْرِهَا، حَتَّى كَانَتْ تِلْكَ الْغَزْوَةُ، غَزَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي حَرٍّ شَدِيدٍ، وَاسْتَقْبَلَ سَفَرًا بَعِيدًا وَمَفَازًا وَعَدُوًّا كَثِيرًا، فَجَلَّى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ أَمْرَهُمْ لِيَتَأَهَّبُوا أُهْبَةَ غَزْوِهِمْ، فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ بِوَجْهِهِ الَّذِي يُرِيدُ، وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَثِيرٌ، وَلاَ يَجْمَعُهُمْ كِتَابٌ حَافِظٌ ـ يُرِيدُ الدِّيوَانَ ـ قَالَ كَعْبٌ فَمَا رَجُلٌ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتَغَيَّبَ إِلاَّ ظَنَّ أَنْ سَيَخْفَى لَهُ مَا لَمْ يَنْزِلْ فِيهِ وَحْىُ اللَّهِ، وَغَزَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم تِلْكَ الْغَزْوَةَ حِينَ طَابَتِ الثِّمَارُ وَالظِّلاَلُ، وَتَجَهَّزَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ مَعَهُ، فَطَفِقْتُ أَغْدُو لِكَىْ أَتَجَهَّزَ مَعَهُمْ فَأَرْجِعُ وَلَمْ أَقْضِ شَيْئًا، فَأَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِي أَنَا قَادِرٌ عَلَيْهِ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَتَمَادَى بِي حَتَّى اشْتَدَّ بِالنَّاسِ الْجِدُّ، فَأَصْبَحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ مَعَهُ وَلَمْ أَقْضِ مِنْ جَهَازِي شَيْئًا، فَقُلْتُ أَتَجَهَّزُ بَعْدَهُ بِيَوْمٍ أَوْ يَوْمَيْنِ ثُمَّ أَلْحَقُهُمْ، فَغَدَوْتُ بَعْدَ أَنْ فَصَلُوا لأَتَجَهَّزَ، فَرَجَعْتُ وَلَمْ أَقْضِ شَيْئًا، ثُمَّ غَدَوْتُ ثُمَّ رَجَعْتُ وَلَمْ أَقْضِ شَيْئًا، فَلَمْ يَزَلْ بِي حَتَّى أَسْرَعُوا وَتَفَارَطَ الْغَزْوُ، وَهَمَمْتُ أَنْ أَرْتَحِلَ فَأُدْرِكَهُمْ، وَلَيْتَنِي فَعَلْتُ، فَلَمْ يُقَدَّرْ لِي ذَلِكَ، فَكُنْتُ إِذَا خَرَجْتُ فِي النَّاسِ بَعْدَ خُرُوجِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَطُفْتُ فِيهِمْ، أَحْزَنَنِي أَنِّي لاَ أَرَى إِلاَّ رَجُلاً مَغْمُوصًا عَلَيْهِ النِّفَاقُ أَوْ رَجُلاً مِمَّنْ عَذَرَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الضُّعَفَاءِ، وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى بَلَغَ تَبُوكَ، فَقَالَ وَهْوَ جَالِسٌ فِي الْقَوْمِ بِتَبُوكَ ‏"‏ مَا فَعَلَ كَعْبٌ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي سَلِمَةَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، حَبَسَهُ بُرْدَاهُ وَنَظَرُهُ فِي عِطْفِهِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ مُعَاذُ بْنُ جَبَلٍ بِئْسَ مَا قُلْتَ، وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ خَيْرًا‏.‏ فَسَكَتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ كَعْبُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ فَلَمَّا بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُ تَوَجَّهَ قَافِلاً حَضَرَنِي هَمِّي، وَطَفِقْتُ أَتَذَكَّرُ الْكَذِبَ وَأَقُولُ بِمَاذَا أَخْرُجُ مِنْ سَخَطِهِ غَدًا وَاسْتَعَنْتُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ بِكُلِّ ذِي رَأْىٍ مِنْ أَهْلِي، فَلَمَّا قِيلَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ أَظَلَّ قَادِمًا زَاحَ عَنِّي الْبَاطِلُ، وَعَرَفْتُ أَنِّي لَنْ أَخْرُجَ مِنْهُ أَبَدًا بِشَىْءٍ فِيهِ كَذِبٌ، فَأَجْمَعْتُ صِدْقَهُ، وَأَصْبَحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَادِمًا، وَكَانَ إِذَا قَدِمَ مِنْ سَفَرٍ بَدَأَ بِالْمَسْجِدِ فَيَرْكَعُ فِيهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ لِلنَّاسِ، فَلَمَّا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ جَاءَهُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ، فَطَفِقُوا يَعْتَذِرُونَ إِلَيْهِ، وَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ، وَكَانُوا بِضْعَةً وَثَمَانِينَ رَجُلاً فَقَبِلَ مِنْهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلاَنِيَتَهُمْ، وَبَايَعَهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمْ، وَوَكَلَ سَرَائِرَهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ، فَجِئْتُهُ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ تَبَسَّمَ تَبَسُّمَ الْمُغْضَبِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ تَعَالَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَجِئْتُ أَمْشِي حَتَّى جَلَسْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، فَقَالَ لِي ‏"‏ مَا خَلَّفَكَ أَلَمْ تَكُنْ قَدِ ابْتَعْتَ ظَهْرَكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ بَلَى، إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لَوْ جَلَسْتُ عِنْدَ غَيْرِكَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا، لَرَأَيْتُ أَنْ سَأَخْرُجُ مِنْ سَخَطِهِ بِعُذْرٍ، وَلَقَدْ أُعْطِيتُ جَدَلاً، وَلَكِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ لَئِنْ حَدَّثْتُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيثَ كَذِبٍ تَرْضَى بِهِ عَنِّي لَيُوشِكَنَّ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُسْخِطَكَ عَلَىَّ، وَلَئِنْ حَدَّثْتُكَ حَدِيثَ صِدْقٍ تَجِدُ عَلَىَّ فِيهِ إِنِّي لأَرْجُو فِيهِ عَفْوَ اللَّهِ، لاَ وَاللَّهِ مَا كَانَ لِي مِنْ عُذْرٍ، وَاللَّهِ مَا كُنْتُ قَطُّ أَقْوَى وَلاَ أَيْسَرَ مِنِّي حِينَ تَخَلَّفْتُ عَنْكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَمَّا هَذَا فَقَدْ صَدَقَ، فَقُمْ حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُمْتُ وَثَارَ رِجَالٌ مِنْ بَنِي سَلِمَةَ فَاتَّبَعُونِي، فَقَالُوا لِي وَاللَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَاكَ كُنْتَ أَذْنَبْتَ ذَنْبًا قَبْلَ هَذَا، وَلَقَدْ عَجَزْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَكُونَ اعْتَذَرْتَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمَا اعْتَذَرَ إِلَيْهِ الْمُتَخَلِّفُونَ، قَدْ كَانَ كَافِيَكَ ذَنْبَكَ اسْتِغْفَارُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَكَ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا زَالُوا يُؤَنِّبُونِي حَتَّى أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَرْجِعَ فَأُكَذِّبُ نَفْسِي، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ لَهُمْ هَلْ لَقِيَ هَذَا مَعِي أَحَدٌ قَالُوا نَعَمْ، رَجُلاَنِ قَالاَ مِثْلَ مَا قُلْتَ، فَقِيلَ لَهُمَا مِثْلُ مَا قِيلَ لَكَ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَنْ هُمَا قَالُوا مُرَارَةُ بْنُ الرَّبِيعِ الْعَمْرِيُّ وَهِلاَلُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ الْوَاقِفِيُّ‏.‏ فَذَكَرُوا لِي رَجُلَيْنِ صَالِحَيْنِ قَدْ شَهِدَا بَدْرًا فِيهِمَا إِسْوَةٌ، فَمَضَيْتُ حِينَ ذَكَرُوهُمَا لِي، وَنَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَنْ كَلاَمِنَا أَيُّهَا الثَّلاَثَةُ مِنْ بَيْنِ مَنْ تَخَلَّفَ عَنْهُ، فَاجْتَنَبَنَا النَّاسُ وَتَغَيَّرُوا لَنَا حَتَّى تَنَكَّرَتْ فِي نَفْسِي الأَرْضُ، فَمَا هِيَ الَّتِي أَعْرِفُ، فَلَبِثْنَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ خَمْسِينَ لَيْلَةً، فَأَمَّا صَاحِبَاىَ فَاسْتَكَانَا وَقَعَدَا فِي بُيُوتِهِمَا يَبْكِيَانِ، وَأَمَّا أَنَا فَكُنْتُ أَشَبَّ الْقَوْمِ وَأَجْلَدَهُمْ، فَكُنْتُ أَخْرُجُ فَأَشْهَدُ الصَّلاَةَ مَعَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَطُوفُ فِي الأَسْوَاقِ، وَلاَ يُكَلِّمُنِي أَحَدٌ، وَآتِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِ وَهْوَ فِي مَجْلِسِهِ بَعْدَ الصَّلاَةِ، فَأَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِي هَلْ حَرَّكَ شَفَتَيْهِ بِرَدِّ السَّلاَمِ عَلَىَّ أَمْ لاَ ثُمَّ أُصَلِّي قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ فَأُسَارِقُهُ النَّظَرَ، فَإِذَا أَقْبَلْتُ عَلَى صَلاَتِي أَقْبَلَ إِلَىَّ، وَإِذَا الْتَفَتُّ نَحْوَهُ أَعْرَضَ عَنِّي، حَتَّى إِذَا طَالَ عَلَىَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ جَفْوَةِ النَّاسِ مَشَيْتُ حَتَّى تَسَوَّرْتُ جِدَارَ حَائِطِ أَبِي قَتَادَةَ وَهْوَ ابْنُ عَمِّي وَأَحَبُّ النَّاسِ إِلَىَّ، فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَدَّ عَلَىَّ السَّلاَمَ، فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا قَتَادَةَ، أَنْشُدُكَ بِاللَّهِ هَلْ تَعْلَمُنِي أُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَسَكَتَ، فَعُدْتُ لَهُ فَنَشَدْتُهُ فَسَكَتَ، فَعُدْتُ لَهُ فَنَشَدْتُهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ‏.‏ فَفَاضَتْ عَيْنَاىَ وَتَوَلَّيْتُ حَتَّى تَسَوَّرْتُ الْجِدَارَ، قَالَ فَبَيْنَا أَنَا أَمْشِي بِسُوقِ الْمَدِينَةِ إِذَا نَبَطِيٌّ مِنْ أَنْبَاطِ أَهْلِ الشَّأْمِ مِمَّنْ قَدِمَ بِالطَّعَامِ يَبِيعُهُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ يَقُولُ مَنْ يَدُلُّ عَلَى كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ فَطَفِقَ النَّاسُ يُشِيرُونَ لَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَنِي دَفَعَ إِلَىَّ كِتَابًا مِنْ مَلِكِ غَسَّانَ، فَإِذَا فِيهِ أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ صَاحِبَكَ قَدْ جَفَاكَ، وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْكَ اللَّهُ بِدَارِ هَوَانٍ وَلاَ مَضْيَعَةٍ، فَالْحَقْ بِنَا نُوَاسِكَ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ لَمَّا قَرَأْتُهَا وَهَذَا أَيْضًا مِنَ الْبَلاَءِ‏.‏ فَتَيَمَّمْتُ بِهَا التَّنُّورَ فَسَجَرْتُهُ بِهَا، حَتَّى إِذَا مَضَتْ أَرْبَعُونَ لَيْلَةً مِنَ الْخَمْسِينَ إِذَا رَسُولُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَأْتِينِي فَقَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ تَعْتَزِلَ امْرَأَتَكَ فَقُلْتُ أُطَلِّقُهَا أَمْ مَاذَا أَفْعَلُ قَالَ لاَ بَلِ اعْتَزِلْهَا وَلاَ تَقْرَبْهَا‏.‏ وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى صَاحِبَىَّ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَقُلْتُ لاِمْرَأَتِي الْحَقِي بِأَهْلِكِ فَتَكُونِي عِنْدَهُمْ حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ فِي هَذَا الأَمْرِ‏.‏ قَالَ كَعْبٌ فَجَاءَتِ امْرَأَةُ هِلاَلِ بْنِ أُمَيَّةَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ هِلاَلَ بْنَ أُمَيَّةَ شَيْخٌ ضَائِعٌ لَيْسَ لَهُ خَادِمٌ فَهَلْ تَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَخْدُمَهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ وَلَكِنْ لاَ يَقْرَبْكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَتْ إِنَّهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا بِهِ حَرَكَةٌ إِلَى شَىْءٍ، وَاللَّهِ مَا زَالَ يَبْكِي مُنْذُ كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ مَا كَانَ إِلَى يَوْمِهِ هَذَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ لِي بَعْضُ أَهْلِي لَوِ اسْتَأْذَنْتَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي امْرَأَتِكَ كَمَا أَذِنَ لاِمْرَأَةِ هِلاَلِ بْنِ أُمَيَّةَ أَنْ تَخْدُمَهُ فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَسْتَأْذِنُ فِيهَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَا يُدْرِينِي مَا يَقُولُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا اسْتَأْذَنْتُهُ فِيهَا وَأَنَا رَجُلٌ شَابٌّ فَلَبِثْتُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَشْرَ لَيَالٍ حَتَّى كَمَلَتْ لَنَا خَمْسُونَ لَيْلَةً مِنْ حِينِ نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ كَلاَمِنَا، فَلَمَّا صَلَّيْتُ صَلاَةَ الْفَجْرِ صُبْحَ خَمْسِينَ لَيْلَةً، وَأَنَا عَلَى ظَهْرِ بَيْتٍ مِنْ بُيُوتِنَا، فَبَيْنَا أَنَا جَالِسٌ عَلَى الْحَالِ الَّتِي ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ، قَدْ ضَاقَتْ عَلَىَّ نَفْسِي، وَضَاقَتْ عَلَىَّ الأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ، سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَ صَارِخٍ أَوْفَى عَلَى جَبَلِ سَلْعٍ بِأَعْلَى صَوْتِهِ يَا كَعْبُ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، أَبْشِرْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَخَرَرْتُ سَاجِدًا، وَعَرَفْتُ أَنْ قَدْ جَاءَ فَرَجٌ، وَآذَنَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِتَوْبَةِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا حِينَ صَلَّى صَلاَةَ الْفَجْرِ، فَذَهَبَ النَّاسُ يُبَشِّرُونَنَا، وَذَهَبَ قِبَلَ صَاحِبَىَّ مُبَشِّرُونَ، وَرَكَضَ إِلَىَّ رَجُلٌ فَرَسًا، وَسَعَى سَاعٍ مِنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأَوْفَى عَلَى الْجَبَلِ وَكَانَ الصَّوْتُ أَسْرَعَ مِنَ الْفَرَسِ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَنِي الَّذِي سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَهُ يُبَشِّرُنِي نَزَعْتُ لَهُ ثَوْبَىَّ، فَكَسَوْتُهُ إِيَّاهُمَا بِبُشْرَاهُ، وَاللَّهِ مَا أَمْلِكُ غَيْرَهُمَا يَوْمَئِذٍ، وَاسْتَعَرْتُ ثَوْبَيْنِ فَلَبِسْتُهُمَا، وَانْطَلَقْتُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَيَتَلَقَّانِي النَّاسُ فَوْجًا فَوْجًا يُهَنُّونِي بِالتَّوْبَةِ، يَقُولُونَ لِتَهْنِكَ تَوْبَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ‏.‏ قَالَ كَعْبٌ حَتَّى دَخَلْتُ الْمَسْجِدَ، فَإِذَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَالِسٌ حَوْلَهُ النَّاسُ فَقَامَ إِلَىَّ طَلْحَةُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ يُهَرْوِلُ حَتَّى صَافَحَنِي وَهَنَّانِي، وَاللَّهِ مَا قَامَ إِلَىَّ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ غَيْرُهُ، وَلاَ أَنْسَاهَا لِطَلْحَةَ، قَالَ كَعْبٌ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهْوَ يَبْرُقُ وَجْهُهُ مِنَ السُّرُورِ ‏"‏ أَبْشِرْ بِخَيْرِ يَوْمٍ مَرَّ عَلَيْكَ مُنْذُ وَلَدَتْكَ أُمُّكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ أَمِنْ عِنْدِكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَمْ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ، بَلْ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا سُرَّ اسْتَنَارَ وَجْهُهُ حَتَّى كَأَنَّهُ قِطْعَةُ قَمَرٍ، وَكُنَّا نَعْرِفُ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ، فَلَمَّا جَلَسْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ مِنْ تَوْبَتِي أَنْ أَنْخَلِعَ مِنْ مَالِي صَدَقَةً إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ‏.‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ بَعْضَ مَالِكَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ فَإِنِّي أُمْسِكُ سَهْمِي الَّذِي بِخَيْبَرَ، فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ إِنَّمَا نَجَّانِي بِالصِّدْقِ، وَإِنَّ مِنْ تَوْبَتِي أَنْ لاَ أُحَدِّثَ إِلاَّ صِدْقًا مَا بَقِيتُ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا أَعْلَمُ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَبْلاَهُ اللَّهُ فِي صِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ مُنْذُ ذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَحْسَنَ مِمَّا أَبْلاَنِي، مَا تَعَمَّدْتُ مُنْذُ ذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى يَوْمِي هَذَا كَذِبًا، وَإِنِّي لأَرْجُو أَنْ يَحْفَظَنِي اللَّهُ فِيمَا بَقِيتُ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏[quran sura="9" aya_start="117" aya_end="119"]{‏لَقَدْ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏[quran sura="9" aya_start="119" aya_end="119"]{‏وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ‏}‏ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ قَطُّ بَعْدَ أَنْ هَدَانِي لِلإِسْلاَمِ أَعْظَمَ فِي نَفْسِي مِنْ صِدْقِي لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ لاَ أَكُونَ كَذَبْتُهُ، فَأَهْلِكَ كَمَا هَلَكَ الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ لِلَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا حِينَ أَنْزَلَ الْوَحْىَ شَرَّ مَا قَالَ لأَحَدٍ، فَقَالَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى ‏[quran sura="9" aya_start="95" aya_end="96"]{‏سَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ إِذَا انْقَلَبْتُمْ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏[quran sura="9" aya_start="96" aya_end="96"]{‏فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَرْضَى عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ كَعْبٌ وَكُنَّا تَخَلَّفْنَا أَيُّهَا الثَّلاَثَةُ عَنْ أَمْرِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ قَبِلَ مِنْهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ حَلَفُوا لَهُ، فَبَايَعَهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمْ وَأَرْجَأَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَمْرَنَا حَتَّى قَضَى اللَّهُ فِيهِ، فَبِذَلِكَ قَالَ اللَّهُ ‏[quran sura="9" aya_start="118" aya_end="118"]{‏وَعَلَى الثَّلاَثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا‏}‏ وَلَيْسَ الَّذِي ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ مِمَّا خُلِّفْنَا عَنِ الْغَزْوِ إِنَّمَا هُوَ تَخْلِيفُهُ إِيَّانَا وَإِرْجَاؤُهُ أَمْرَنَا عَمَّنْ حَلَفَ لَهُ وَاعْتَذَرَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَبِلَ مِنْهُ‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, that ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, who used to lead Ka‘b, his father’s son, when he became blind, said: I heard Ka‘b ibn Malik tell the story of his staying behind from the expedition to Tabuk. Ka‘b said: I never stayed behind from an expedition the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, undertook except the expedition to Tabuk. I had also stayed behind from the expedition of Badr, but the Prophet did not reproach anyone who had stayed behind from it. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had set out intending to intercept the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy unexpectedly. I had been present with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on the Night of al-‘Aqabah, when we pledged firmly to follow Islam. I would not trade being present there for being present at Badr, even though Badr is more widely remembered among people. My circumstances when I stayed behind from that expedition were that I had never been stronger or more prosperous. By Allah, before that I had never owned two riding camels at once, but I had both of them for that expedition. Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended an expedition, he would conceal his real destination by indicating another one. But when that expedition came, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, undertook it in intense heat, facing a long journey through desert and a numerous enemy. He made the destination clear to the Muslims so they could prepare properly for the expedition, and told them where he intended to go. The Muslims with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, were numerous, and they were not all listed in an official register. Ka‘b said: A man who wanted to stay behind would think that he could remain hidden unless Allah revealed something about him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, set out on that expedition when the fruit was ripe and the shade was pleasant. The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims with him prepared themselves. I would go out in the morning intending to prepare with them, then return having done nothing. I would tell myself, ‘I can do it.’ This continued until the people became serious about the expedition. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and the Muslims with him set out, while I had done none of my preparations. I said, ‘I will prepare a day or two after they leave, then catch up with them.’ I went out the morning after they had departed to prepare, then returned having done nothing. I went out again, then returned having done nothing. This went on until they had hastened away and the expedition had passed me by. I considered setting out to catch them, and I wish I had done so, but it was not destined for me. After the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had departed, whenever I went out among the people, it grieved me that I saw no one there except a man suspected of hypocrisy or a man among the weak whom Allah had excused. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. As he sat among the people in Tabuk, he asked, ‘What has happened to Ka‘b?’ A man from Banu Salimah said, ‘Messenger of Allah, his two fine garments and his admiration of himself have kept him back.’ Mu‘adh ibn Jabal said, ‘What a bad thing you have said! By Allah, Messenger of Allah, we know nothing about him except good.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said nothing. Ka‘b ibn Malik said: When I heard that he was returning, worry came over me. I began thinking of lies and asking myself what excuse I could use to escape his displeasure the next day. I sought advice from every sensible person in my family. But when I heard that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was close to arriving, falsehood left me. I knew that I could never get out of this by saying something false, so I resolved to tell the truth. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, arrived in the morning. When he returned from a journey, he would begin by going to the mosque, pray two units there, then sit down to meet the people. When he had done this, the men who had stayed behind came and began making excuses to him and swearing oaths. They were a little more than eighty men. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, accepted what they showed outwardly, accepted their pledges, and asked Allah to forgive them, leaving what was hidden in their hearts to Allah. I came to him. When I greeted him, he smiled with the smile of an angry man and said, ‘Come here.’ I walked over and sat before him. He said to me, ‘What kept you back? Had you not bought a riding camel?’ I said, ‘Yes. By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else in this world, I would think that I could escape his displeasure with an excuse. I have been given the ability to argue persuasively. But by Allah, I know that if I tell you a lie today that pleases you, Allah will soon make you angry with me. If I tell you the truth, which will make you angry with me, I hope for Allah’s forgiveness. By Allah, I had no excuse. I had never been stronger or more prosperous than when I stayed behind.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘As for this man, he has told the truth. Get up and wait until Allah decides your case.’ I got up. Some men from Banu Salimah followed me and said, ‘By Allah, we never knew that you had committed a sin before this. You were unable to make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, like the excuses the others who stayed behind made. The Messenger of Allah’s asking forgiveness for you would have been enough for your sin.’ By Allah, they kept reproaching me until I wanted to go back and contradict myself. Then I asked them, ‘Did anyone else meet the same response as I did?’ They said, ‘Yes. Two men said the same as you, and they were told what you were told.’ I asked, ‘Who are they?’ They said, ‘Murarah ibn al-Rabi‘ al-‘Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi.’ They named two righteous men who had been present at Badr, examples for me to follow. I continued on after they named them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, forbade the Muslims to speak to the three of us, out of all those who had stayed behind. People avoided us and changed their attitude toward us, until the land itself seemed strange to me and no longer the land I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. My two companions gave in and stayed in their homes, weeping. I was the youngest and strongest of the group. I would go out, pray with the Muslims, and walk through the markets, but no one would speak to me. I would go to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he sat with people after prayer, greet him, and wonder to myself whether he had moved his lips to return my greeting. I would pray close to him and steal glances at him. When I turned toward my prayer, he would face me; when I turned toward him, he would turn away from me. When people’s coldness toward me had lasted a long time, I walked until I climbed over the wall into the garden of Abu Qatadah, my cousin and the person I loved most. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said, ‘Abu Qatadah, I ask you by Allah: do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?’ He remained silent. I asked him again, and he remained silent. I asked a third time, and he said, ‘Allah and His Messenger know best.’ My eyes overflowed with tears, and I turned away and climbed back over the wall. As I was walking through the market of Madinah, a Nabatean from among the people of Syria, who had brought food to sell in Madinah, began asking, ‘Who can direct me to Ka‘b ibn Malik?’ People started pointing him toward me. When he came to me, he handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. It said: ‘To continue: I have heard that your companion has treated you harshly. Allah has not placed you in a land of humiliation and neglect. Come to us, and we will comfort you.’ When I read it, I said, ‘This too is a trial.’ I went with it to the oven and burned it. When forty of the fifty nights had passed, a messenger from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to me and said, ‘The Messenger of Allah commands you to keep away from your wife.’ I asked, ‘Should I divorce her, or what should I do?’ He said, ‘No. Just stay apart from her and do not go near her.’ He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife, ‘Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter.’ Ka‘b said: The wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is an old, helpless man with no servant. Would you dislike it if I served him?’ He said, ‘No, but he must not come near you.’ She said, ‘By Allah, he has no desire or strength for anything. By Allah, he has done nothing but weep from the day his case began until this day.’ Someone from my family said to me, ‘Why don’t you ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, for permission concerning your wife, as he gave Hilal ibn Umayyah’s wife permission to serve him?’ I said, ‘By Allah, I will not ask the Messenger of Allah for permission about her. How do I know what the Messenger of Allah would say if I asked him about her, when I am a young man?’ I remained in that state for ten more nights, completing fifty nights since the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had forbidden people to speak to us. When I had prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of the fiftieth night, I was on the roof of one of our houses. I sat in the state Allah had described: my soul had become constricted, and the earth, vast as it was, had become constricted for me. I heard the voice of someone calling from the top of Mount Sal‘, shouting at the top of his voice, ‘Ka‘b ibn Malik, rejoice!’ I fell down in prostration, knowing that relief had come. After the dawn prayer, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, announced that Allah had accepted our repentance. People went to bring us the good news. Some went to my two companions. A man rode a horse toward me, and another man from Aslam ran up the mountain to call me. The voice was faster than the horse. When the man whose voice I had heard came to bring me the good news, I took off my two garments and gave them to him for his good news. By Allah, I owned nothing else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on, then set out for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. People came to meet me in groups, congratulating me on my repentance and saying, ‘May Allah’s acceptance of your repentance bring you joy.’ Ka‘b said: I entered the mosque and found the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sitting with people around him. Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd Allah got up and hurried toward me, shook my hand, and congratulated me. By Allah, no other man from the Emigrants got up for me, and I will never forget that kindness from Talhah. When I greeted the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his face shining with joy, he said, ‘Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother gave birth to you.’ I asked, ‘Is this from you, Messenger of Allah, or from Allah?’ He said, ‘No, rather it is from Allah.’ When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was happy, his face would shine until it looked like a piece of the moon, and we could recognize that in him. When I sat before him, I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, as part of my repentance I will give up some of my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Keep some of your wealth; that will be better for you.’ I said, ‘Then I will keep my share at Khaybar.’ I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Allah saved me only because I told the truth. Part of my repentance is that for the rest of my life I will speak only the truth.’ By Allah, I know of no Muslim whom Allah has tested with truthful speech since I told that to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, more favorably than He tested me. From the time I said that to the Messenger of Allah until this day, I have never deliberately told a lie, and I hope that Allah will protect me for the rest of my life. Allah revealed to His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ‘Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Emigrants…’ through the words ‘and be with the truthful’ (9:117–119). By Allah, after Allah guided me to Islam, He has never granted me a blessing greater in my eyes than my having told the truth to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and not lied to him and perished as those who lied perished. When Allah sent down revelation about those who lied, He said the worst thing He said about anyone. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said, ‘They will swear by Allah to you when you return…’ through the words ‘Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people’ (9:95–96). Ka‘b said: We three had stayed behind, unlike those whose excuses and oaths the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, accepted. He accepted their pledges, asked Allah to forgive them, and left their hidden matters to Allah. He deferred our case until Allah decided it. That is why Allah said, ‘And [He also turned in mercy] to the three who were left behind’ (9:118). What Allah meant was not that we had been left behind from the expedition. Rather, He left our cases pending and deferred them apart from those who had sworn to him and made excuses that he accepted.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4551, book 65, باب ‏ {‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلاً أُولَئِكَ لاَ خَلاَقَ لَهُمْ‏} ‏ لاَ خَيْرَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيٌّ ـ هُوَ ابْنُ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ ـ سَمِعَ هُشَيْمًا، أَخْبَرَنَا الْعَوَّامُ بْنُ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أَوْفَى ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ رَجُلاً، أَقَامَ سِلْعَةً فِي السُّوقِ فَحَلَفَ فِيهَا لَقَدْ أَعْطَى بِهَا مَا لَمْ يُعْطَهُ‏.‏ لِيُوقِعَ فِيهَا رَجُلاً مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، فَنَزَلَتْ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="77" aya_end="77"]{‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلاً‏}‏ إِلَى آخِرِ الآيَةِ‏.‏
en_text: Ali—namely, the son of Abu Hashim—narrated to us: He heard Hushaym. Al-‘Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man displayed some merchandise in the market and swore about it that he had been offered a price for it that he had not in fact been offered, in order to entice one of the Muslims to buy it. Then the verse, ‘Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a small price…’ (3:77), through the end of the verse, was revealed.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4552, book 65, باب ‏ {‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلاً أُولَئِكَ لاَ خَلاَقَ لَهُمْ‏} ‏ لاَ خَيْرَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا نَصْرُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ نَصْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ دَاوُدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، أَنَّ امْرَأَتَيْنِ، كَانَتَا تَخْرِزَانِ فِي بَيْتٍ ـ أَوْ فِي الْحُجْرَةِ ـ فَخَرَجَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا وَقَدْ أُنْفِذَ بِإِشْفًى فِي كَفِّهَا، فَادَّعَتْ عَلَى الأُخْرَى، فَرُفِعَ إِلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَوْ يُعْطَى النَّاسُ بِدَعْوَاهُمْ لَذَهَبَ دِمَاءُ قَوْمٍ وَأَمْوَالُهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ذَكِّرُوهَا بِاللَّهِ وَاقْرَءُوا عَلَيْهَا ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="77" aya_end="77"]{‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ‏}‏‏.‏ فَذَكَّرُوهَا فَاعْتَرَفَتْ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ الْيَمِينُ عَلَى الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Nasr ibn Ali ibn Nasr narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, that two women were sewing in a house—or in a room. One of them came out with an awl driven through the palm of her hand and accused the other. The case was brought before Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn ‘Abbas said that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘If people were given what they claimed, the lives and property of a people would be lost.’ He told them, ‘Remind her of Allah and recite to her, “Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant…”’ (3:77). They reminded her, and she confessed. Ibn ‘Abbas then said that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4553, book 65, باب ‏{‏قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ لاَ نَعْبُدَ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ،‏.‏ وَحَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو سُفْيَانَ، مِنْ فِيهِ إِلَى فِيَّ قَالَ انْطَلَقْتُ فِي الْمُدَّةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَالَ ـ فَبَيْنَا أَنَا بِالشَّأْمِ إِذْ جِيءَ بِكِتَابٍ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى هِرَقْلَ قَالَ وَكَانَ دِحْيَةُ الْكَلْبِيُّ جَاءَ بِهِ فَدَفَعَهُ إِلَى عَظِيمِ بُصْرَى، فَدَفَعَهُ عَظِيمُ بُصْرَى إِلَى ـ هِرَقْلَ ـ قَالَ فَقَالَ هِرَقْلُ هَلْ هَا هُنَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ قَوْمِ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ فَقَالُوا نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَدُعِيتُ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ فَدَخَلْنَا عَلَى هِرَقْلَ، فَأُجْلِسْنَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقَالَ أَيُّكُمْ أَقْرَبُ نَسَبًا مِنْ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ فَقَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَقُلْتُ أَنَا‏.‏ فَأَجْلَسُونِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، وَأَجْلَسُوا أَصْحَابِي خَلْفِي، ثُمَّ دَعَا بِتُرْجُمَانِهِ فَقَالَ قُلْ لَهُمْ إِنِّي سَائِلٌ هَذَا عَنْ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ، فَإِنْ كَذَبَنِي فَكَذِّبُوهُ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَايْمُ اللَّهِ، لَوْلاَ أَنْ يُؤْثِرُوا عَلَىَّ الْكَذِبَ لَكَذَبْتُ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِتُرْجُمَانِهِ سَلْهُ كَيْفَ حَسَبُهُ فِيكُمْ قَالَ قُلْتُ هُوَ فِينَا ذُو حَسَبٍ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ كَانَ مِنْ آبَائِهِ مَلِكٌ قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ كُنْتُمْ تَتَّهِمُونَهُ بِالْكَذِبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقُولَ مَا قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ أَيَتَّبِعُهُ أَشْرَافُ النَّاسِ أَمْ ضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ قَالَ قُلْتُ بَلْ ضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ يَزِيدُونَ أَوْ يَنْقُصُونَ قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ بَلْ يَزِيدُونَ‏.‏ قَالَ هَلْ يَرْتَدُّ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ، بَعْدَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فِيهِ، سَخْطَةً لَهُ قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ قَاتَلْتُمُوهُ قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ قِتَالُكُمْ إِيَّاهُ قَالَ قُلْتُ تَكُونُ الْحَرْبُ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُ سِجَالاً، يُصِيبُ مِنَّا وَنُصِيبُ مِنْهُ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ يَغْدِرُ قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ وَنَحْنُ مِنْهُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةِ لاَ نَدْرِي مَا هُوَ صَانِعٌ فِيهَا‏.‏ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَمْكَنَنِي مِنْ كَلِمَةٍ أُدْخِلُ فِيهَا شَيْئًا غَيْرَ هَذِهِ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ قَالَ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ أَحَدٌ قَبْلَهُ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِتُرْجُمَانِهِ قُلْ لَهُ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ حَسَبِهِ فِيكُمْ، فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّهُ فِيكُمْ ذُو حَسَبٍ، وَكَذَلِكَ الرُّسُلُ تُبْعَثُ فِي أَحْسَابِ قَوْمِهَا، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ كَانَ فِي آبَائِهِ مَلِكٌ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ فَقُلْتُ لَوْ كَانَ مِنْ آبَائِهِ مَلِكٌ قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ يَطْلُبُ مُلْكَ آبَائِهِ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ أَتْبَاعِهِ أَضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ أَمْ أَشْرَافُهُمْ فَقُلْتَ بَلْ ضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ، وَهُمْ أَتْبَاعُ الرُّسُلِ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ كُنْتُمْ تَتَّهِمُونَهُ بِالْكَذِبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقُولَ مَا قَالَ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، فَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيَدَعَ الْكَذِبَ عَلَى النَّاسِ ثُمَّ يَذْهَبَ فَيَكْذِبَ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ يَرْتَدُّ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فِيهِ سَخْطَةً لَهُ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، وَكَذَلِكَ الإِيمَانُ إِذَا خَالَطَ بَشَاشَةَ الْقُلُوبِ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ يَزِيدُونَ أَمْ يَنْقُصُونَ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّهُمْ يَزِيدُونَ، وَكَذَلِكَ الإِيمَانُ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ قَاتَلْتُمُوهُ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّكُمْ قَاتَلْتُمُوهُ فَتَكُونُ الْحَرْبُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ سِجَالاً، يَنَالُ مِنْكُمْ وَتَنَالُونَ مِنْهُ، وَكَذَلِكَ الرُّسُلُ تُبْتَلَى، ثُمَّ تَكُونُ لَهُمُ الْعَاقِبَةُ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ يَغْدِرُ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّهُ لاَ يَغْدِرُ، وَكَذَلِكَ الرُّسُلُ لاَ تَغْدِرُ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ قَالَ أَحَدٌ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ قَبْلَهُ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، فَقُلْتُ لَوْ كَانَ قَالَ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ أَحَدٌ قَبْلَهُ قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ ائْتَمَّ بِقَوْلٍ قِيلَ قَبْلَهُ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ قَالَ بِمَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ قَالَ قُلْتُ يَأْمُرُنَا بِالصَّلاَةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ وَالصِّلَةِ وَالْعَفَافِ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنْ يَكُ مَا تَقُولُ فِيهِ حَقًّا فَإِنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ، وَقَدْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ خَارِجٌ، وَلَمْ أَكُ أَظُنُّهُ مِنْكُمْ، وَلَوْ أَنِّي أَعْلَمُ أَنِّي أَخْلُصُ إِلَيْهِ لأَحْبَبْتُ لِقَاءَهُ، وَلَوْ كُنْتُ عِنْدَهُ لَغَسَلْتُ عَنْ قَدَمَيْهِ، وَلَيَبْلُغَنَّ مُلْكُهُ مَا تَحْتَ قَدَمَىَّ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِكِتَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَرَأَهُ، فَإِذَا فِيهِ ‏"‏ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، إِلَى هِرَقْلَ عَظِيمِ الرُّومِ، سَلاَمٌ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى، أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنِّي أَدْعُوكَ بِدِعَايَةِ الإِسْلاَمِ، أَسْلِمْ تَسْلَمْ، وَأَسْلِمْ يُؤْتِكَ اللَّهُ أَجْرَكَ مَرَّتَيْنِ، فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ إِثْمَ الأَرِيسِيِّينَ، وَ‏{‏يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ لاَ نَعْبُدَ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="64" aya_end="64"]{‏اشْهَدُوا بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ‏}‏‏"‏‏.‏ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَةِ الْكِتَابِ ارْتَفَعَتِ الأَصْوَاتُ عِنْدَهُ، وَكَثُرَ اللَّغَطُ، وَأُمِرَ بِنَا فَأُخْرِجْنَا قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لأَصْحَابِي حِينَ خَرَجْنَا لَقَدْ أَمِرَ أَمْرُ ابْنِ أَبِي كَبْشَةَ، أَنَّهُ لَيَخَافُهُ مَلِكُ بَنِي الأَصْفَرِ فَمَا زِلْتُ مُوقِنًا بِأَمْرِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ سَيَظْهَرُ حَتَّى أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ الإِسْلاَمَ‏.‏ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ فَدَعَا هِرَقْلُ عُظَمَاءَ الرُّومِ فَجَمَعَهُمْ فِي دَارٍ لَهُ فَقَالَ يَا مَعْشَرَ الرُّومِ، هَلْ لَكُمْ فِي الْفَلاَحِ وَالرَّشَدِ آخِرَ الأَبَدِ، وَأَنْ يَثْبُتَ لَكُمْ مُلْكُكُمْ قَالَ فَحَاصُوا حَيْصَةَ حُمُرِ الْوَحْشِ إِلَى الأَبْوَابِ، فَوَجَدُوهَا قَدْ غُلِقَتْ، فَقَالَ عَلَىَّ بِهِمْ‏.‏ فَدَعَا بِهِمْ فَقَالَ إِنِّي إِنَّمَا اخْتَبَرْتُ شِدَّتَكُمْ عَلَى دِينِكُمْ، فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ مِنْكُمُ الَّذِي أَحْبَبْتُ‏.‏ فَسَجَدُوا لَهُ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ‏.‏
en_text: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to me, from Hisham, from Ma‘mar. And ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah informed me, saying: Ibn ‘Abbas narrated to me, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, speaking directly to me. He said: During the period of truce between me and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, I set out. While I was in Syria, a letter from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was brought to Heraclius. Dihyah al-Kalbi had brought it and handed it to the governor of Busra, who then handed it to Heraclius. Heraclius said, ‘Is there anyone here from the people of this man who claims to be a prophet?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ I was summoned with a group of Quraysh, and we entered to see Heraclius. He seated us before him and said, ‘Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?’ Abu Sufyan said: I replied, ‘I am.’ They seated me before him and placed my companions behind me. Then he summoned his interpreter and said, ‘Tell them that I am going to question this man about the man who claims to be a prophet. If he lies to me, tell me that he is lying.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, had I not been afraid that they would report my lie, I would have lied. Then Heraclius said to his interpreter, ‘Ask him: What is his standing among you?’ I replied, ‘He is of noble standing among us.’ He asked, ‘Was any of his forefathers a king?’ I replied, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he has said?’ I replied, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Do the nobles follow him, or the weak?’ I replied, ‘Rather, the weak.’ He asked, ‘Are they increasing or decreasing?’ I replied, ‘They are increasing.’ He asked, ‘Does anyone among them abandon his religion out of resentment after entering it?’ I replied, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Have you fought him?’ I replied, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘How has the fighting between you and him gone?’ I replied, ‘The war between us and him has gone back and forth: sometimes he has prevailed against us, and sometimes we have prevailed against him.’ He asked, ‘Does he betray?’ I replied, ‘No. During this period of truce with him, we do not know what he will do.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, I could find no opportunity to add anything against him except that one remark. Heraclius asked, ‘Has anyone before him made this claim?’ I replied, ‘No.’ Then he said to his interpreter, ‘Tell him: I asked you about his standing among you, and you claimed that he is of noble standing among you. That is how messengers are sent from among the noble of their people. I asked whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you claimed that there was not. I said that if one of his forefathers had been a king, I would have thought that he was a man seeking his forefathers’ kingdom. I asked whether his followers were the weak or the nobles, and you said they were the weak; those are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether you had accused him of lying before he said what he has said, and you claimed that you had not. So I know that he would not leave lying to people and then go and lie about Allah. I asked whether anyone among them abandons his religion out of resentment after entering it, and you claimed that no one does. Such is faith when its delight enters the hearts. I asked whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you claimed they are increasing. Such is faith until it becomes complete. I asked whether you had fought him, and you claimed that you had, and that the war between you and him had gone back and forth: sometimes he prevailed against you and sometimes you prevailed against him. Such is the trial of messengers; then the outcome is theirs. I asked whether he betrays, and you claimed that he does not. Such is the way of messengers: they do not betray. I asked whether anyone before him had made this claim, and you claimed that no one had. I said that if anyone before him had made this claim, I would have thought that he was following a claim made before him.’ Then Heraclius said, ‘What does he command you to do?’ I replied, ‘He commands us to pray, give zakat, maintain ties of kinship, and remain chaste.’ He said, ‘If what you say about him is true, then he is a prophet. I knew that he would appear, but I did not think that he would be from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would love to meet him. If I were with him, I would wash his feet. His dominion will surely reach what is beneath my feet.’ Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and read it. It said: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: I call you with the call of Islam. Submit, and you will be safe. Submit, and Allah will give you your reward twice over. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the ploughmen. “O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah…”’ through His words, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims’ (3:64). When he finished reading the letter, voices rose around him and the clamor grew loud. We were ordered out. Abu Sufyan said: When we came out, I said to my companions, ‘The matter of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become tremendous. The king of the Banu al-Asfar fears him.’ I remained certain that the matter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would prevail until Allah brought Islam into my heart. Al-Zuhri said: Heraclius summoned the leading Romans and gathered them in a house of his. He said, ‘O Romans, would you like lasting success and right guidance, and for your kingdom to remain firmly established?’ They rushed toward the doors like wild donkeys, but found them locked. He said, ‘Bring them back to me.’ They were brought back, and he said, ‘I only tested how firmly you hold to your religion. I have now seen what I wanted to see from you.’ They prostrated to him and were pleased with him.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4554, book 65, باب ‏ {‏لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ‏} ‏ إِلَى ‏{‏بِهِ عَلِيمٌ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ يَقُولُ كَانَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ أَكْثَرَ أَنْصَارِيٍّ بِالْمَدِينَةِ نَخْلاً، وَكَانَ أَحَبَّ أَمْوَالِهِ إِلَيْهِ بَيْرُحَاءٍ، وَكَانَتْ مُسْتَقْبِلَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ، وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدْخُلُهَا وَيَشْرَبُ مِنْ مَاءٍ فِيهَا طَيِّبٍ، فَلَمَّا أُنْزِلَتْ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="92" aya_end="92"]{‏لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ‏}‏ قَامَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="92" aya_end="92"]{‏لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ‏}‏ وَإِنَّ أَحَبَّ أَمْوَالِي إِلَىَّ بَيْرُحَاءٍ وَإِنَّهَا صَدَقَةٌ لِلَّهِ، أَرْجُو بِرَّهَا وَذُخْرَهَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، فَضَعْهَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ حَيْثُ أَرَاكَ اللَّهُ‏.‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ بَخْ، ذَلِكَ مَالٌ رَايِحٌ، ذَلِكَ مَالٌ رَايِحٌ، وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُ مَا قُلْتَ، وَإِنِّي أَرَى أَنْ تَجْعَلَهَا فِي الأَقْرَبِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ أَفْعَلُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَقَسَمَهَا أَبُو طَلْحَةَ فِي أَقَارِبِهِ وَبَنِي عَمِّهِ‏.‏ قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ وَرَوْحُ بْنُ عُبَادَةَ ‏"‏ ذَلِكَ مَالٌ رَابِحٌ ‏"‏‏.‏ حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى قَالَ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى مَالِكٍ ‏"‏ مَالٌ رَايِحٌ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Isma‘il narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Abu Talhah had more date palms than any of the Ansar in Madinah. The most beloved of his possessions to him was Bayruha’, which faced the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to enter it and drink from its pleasant water. When the verse, ‘You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love’ (3:92), was revealed, Abu Talhah stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Allah says, “You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love” (3:92). The most beloved of my possessions to me is Bayruha’. It is charity for Allah, and I hope for its goodness and its store of reward with Allah. So place it, Messenger of Allah, wherever Allah shows you.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Well done! That is a profitable possession; that is a profitable possession. I have heard what you said, and I think you should give it to your closest relatives.’ Abu Talhah said, ‘I will do that, Messenger of Allah.’ Abu Talhah then divided it among his relatives and his paternal cousins. ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf and Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah said, ‘That is a profit-bearing possession.’ Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: I read to Malik, ‘A profitable possession.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4555, book 65, باب ‏ {‏لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ‏} ‏ إِلَى ‏{‏بِهِ عَلِيمٌ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الأَنْصَارِيُّ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي، عَنْ ثُمَامَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ فَجَعَلَهَا لِحَسَّانَ وَأُبِيٍّ، وَأَنَا أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ، وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ لِي مِنْهَا شَيْئًا‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Thumamah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: He gave it to Hassan and Ubayy, although I was closer to him, and he gave me none of it.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4556, book 65, باب ‏ {‏قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَاتْلُوهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ‏} ‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ الْمُنْذِرِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو ضَمْرَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ عُقْبَةَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ الْيَهُودَ، جَاءُوا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِرَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ وَامْرَأَةٍ قَدْ زَنَيَا، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ ‏"‏ كَيْفَ تَفْعَلُونَ بِمَنْ زَنَى مِنْكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا نُحَمِّمُهُمَا وَنَضْرِبُهُمَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ تَجِدُونَ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ الرَّجْمَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا لاَ نَجِدُ فِيهَا شَيْئًا‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سَلاَمٍ كَذَبْتُمْ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="93" aya_end="93"]{‏فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَاتْلُوهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ‏}‏ فَوَضَعَ مِدْرَاسُهَا الَّذِي يُدَرِّسُهَا مِنْهُمْ كَفَّهُ عَلَى آيَةِ الرَّجْمِ، فَطَفِقَ يَقْرَأُ مَا دُونَ يَدِهِ وَمَا وَرَاءَهَا، وَلاَ يَقْرَأُ آيَةَ الرَّجْمِ، فَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ عَنْ آيَةِ الرَّجْمِ فَقَالَ مَا هَذِهِ فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا ذَلِكَ قَالُوا هِيَ آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا فَرُجِمَا قَرِيبًا مِنْ حَيْثُ مَوْضِعُ الْجَنَائِزِ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ، فَرَأَيْتُ صَاحِبَهَا يَجْنَأُ عَلَيْهَا يَقِيهَا الْحِجَارَةَ‏.‏
en_text: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me: Abu Damrah narrated to us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Jews brought to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery. He asked them, ‘What do you do with someone among you who commits adultery?’ They said, ‘We blacken their faces and beat them.’ He said, ‘Do you not find stoning in the Torah?’ They said, ‘We find nothing in it.’ ‘Abd Allah ibn Salam said to them, ‘You have lied. Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful’ (3:93). Their Torah scholar, who taught it to them, placed his hand over the verse about stoning and began reading what was before and after his hand, but he did not read the verse about stoning. He moved his hand away from the verse about stoning, and the Prophet said, ‘What is this?’ When they saw that, they said, ‘It is the verse about stoning.’ He ordered that the two be stoned near the place where the funeral biers were by the mosque. I saw the man bend over the woman, shielding her from the stones.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4557, book 65, باب ‏ {‏كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ‏} ‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، عَنْ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَة َ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="110" aya_end="110"]{‏كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ‏}‏ قَالَ خَيْرَ النَّاسِ لِلنَّاسِ، تَأْتُونَ بِهِمْ فِي السَّلاَسِلِ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ حَتَّى يَدْخُلُوا فِي الإِسْلاَمِ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Maysarah, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the verse, ‘You are the best community brought forth for mankind’ (3:110). He said: They are the best of people for mankind; you bring them with chains around their necks until they enter Islam.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4558, book 65, باب ‏ {‏إِذْ هَمَّتْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ تَفْشَلاَ‏} ‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ قَالَ عَمْرٌو سَمِعْتُ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّه ِ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ يَقُولُ فِينَا نَزَلَتْ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="122" aya_end="122"]{‏إِذْ هَمَّتْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ تَفْشَلاَ وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا‏}‏ قَالَ نَحْنُ الطَّائِفَتَانِ بَنُو حَارِثَةَ وَبَنُو سَلِمَةَ، وَمَا نُحِبُّ ـ وَقَالَ سُفْيَانُ مَرَّةً وَمَا يَسُرُّنِي ـ أَنَّهَا لَمْ تُنْزَلْ لِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="122" aya_end="122"]{‏وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا‏}‏
en_text: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: ‘Amr said, ‘I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: “When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their protector” (3:122) was revealed concerning us. He said: We were the two groups, Banu Harithah and Banu Salimah. We would not like—or Sufyan once said, ‘It would not please me’—for it not to have been revealed, because Allah says, ‘though Allah was their protector’ (3:122).’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4559, book 65, باب ‏{‏لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا حِبَّانُ بْنُ مُوسَى، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي سَالِمٌ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ الْعَنْ فُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا ‏"‏‏.‏ بَعْدَ مَا يَقُولُ ‏"‏ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ رَبَّنَا وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏[quran sura="3" aya_start="128" aya_end="128"]{‏فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ‏}‏‏.‏ رَوَاهُ إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ رَاشِدٍ عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ‏.‏
en_text: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when he raised his head from bowing in the final unit of the dawn prayer, say, after saying, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, to You belongs all praise’: ‘O Allah, curse so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so.’ Then Allah revealed, ‘You have no part in the matter…’ through His words, ‘for indeed, they are wrongdoers’ (3:128). Ishaq ibn Rashid also narrated it from al-Zuhri.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 4560, book 65, باب ‏{‏لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ، وَأَبِي، سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ عَلَى أَحَدٍ أَوْ يَدْعُوَ لأَحَدٍ قَنَتَ بَعْدَ الرُّكُوعِ، فَرُبَّمَا قَالَ إِذَا قَالَ ‏"‏ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ، اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْجِ الْوَلِيدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ، وَسَلَمَةَ بْنَ هِشَامٍ، وَعَيَّاشَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ، اللَّهُمَّ اشْدُدْ وَطْأَتَكَ عَلَى مُضَرَ وَاجْعَلْهَا سِنِينَ كَسِنِي يُوسُفَ ‏"‏‏.‏ يَجْهَرُ بِذَلِكَ وَكَانَ يَقُولُ فِي بَعْضِ صَلاَتِهِ فِي صَلاَةِ الْفَجْرِ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ الْعَنْ فُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا ‏"‏‏.‏ لأَحْيَاءٍ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ، حَتَّى أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ‏}‏ الآيَةَ‏.‏
en_text: Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us: Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, wanted to supplicate against someone or for someone, he would perform the qunut supplication after bowing. Sometimes, after saying, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him; O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise,’ he would say, ‘O Allah, rescue al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, and ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah. O Allah, intensify Your punishment upon Mudar and make it years like the years of Yusuf.’ He would say this aloud. During some of his prayers, in the dawn prayer, he would say, ‘O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so,’ referring to clans among the Arabs, until Allah revealed the verse, ‘You have no part in the matter…’ (3:128).
